However, for motion control problems, where the reference signal is time-varying, it is not straightforward to design control laws for such pH systems that still provides an insightful energy interpretation of the closed-loop system. One major difficulty is that the external reference signals can induce both the closed-loop system and total energy function to be time-varying. In this case, the closed-loop system may not be dissipative, or if it is a time-varying dissipative system, the usual La-Salle invariance principle argument can no longer be invoked for analyzing the asymptotic behavior.
